edbDesc: The property of some non-Newtonian pseudoplastic fluids to show a time-dependent change in viscosity; the longer the fluid undergoes shear stress, the lower its viscosity. A thixotropic fluid is a fluid which takes a finite amount of time to attain equilibrium viscosity when introduced to a step change in shear rate. Many gels and colloids are thixotropic materials, exhibiting a stable form at rest but becoming fluid when agitated.
title: Thixotropy
description: Some thick gels turn runny when shaken or stirred and slowly set again when left alone. Schalek and Szegvári found iron-oxide gels doing this in 1923; it's why non-drip paint brushes on smoothly yet stays put on a wall, and why drilling mud holds rock chips up when the pumps stop.
effect: a gel thins when stirred and thickens again at rest
strength: Non-drip paint thick enough to stand on a vertical wall thins under a brush in a second and stiffens again within a minute.
pickWhy: Specific named effect with clear jobs, distinct from shear thickening; date from Schalek and Szegvári's gels, the name came from Freundlich's lab in 1927.
